resourceProfile.tip.players: External applications to open playable files. You can assign different players for different file extensions. By default, the system's default application is used to open playable files.
resourceProfile.tip.properties: Choose the properties used in resource details and set their value-source order. Unlinking never deletes a property or its saved values.

enhancementConfig.title: Configure metadata enhancement
enhancementConfig.selectGroupFirst: Please select at least one resource type first
enhancementConfig.dynamicHint: {{enhancers}} in this group support dynamic properties. Click the configure button below to add more properties.
enhancementConfig.dynamicExplanation: Dynamic properties are extracted at runtime by enhancers from their data sources, such as properties in the left panel of Bangumi pages, properties on the right side of DLsite covers, and regex capture groups. You need to configure the corresponding enhancer first. Once configured, dynamic properties will appear in the list below.
enhancementConfig.configureDynamicEnhanc: Configure enhancers that support dynamic properties
enhancementConfig.noDynamicPropertiesYet: No dynamic properties configured yet. Please configure the enhancers above first.
enhancementConfig.unboundWarning: This property is checked but not bound to any system property. Enhanced data won't be applied. Click the button to bind or create a property, or uncheck it.
enhancementConfig.unboundBlockHint: {{count}} enabled enhancement target(s) have no bound property; cannot save until each is either bound or unchecked.
enhancementConfig.intro: Enhancers automatically fetch and populate resource properties from external data sources (e.g. Bangumi, DLsite). Select a resource type, check the properties and sources you need, then bind them to system properties.
enhancementConfig.introStep1: Select a resource type to see available properties
enhancementConfig.introStep2: Check the data sources (enhancers) for each property — select multiple for fallback
enhancementConfig.introStep3: Bind properties to make enhanced data visible on resources
enhancementConfig.validation.title: Enhancer Configuration Validation
enhancementConfig.validation.description: Select a resource to validate the current enhancer configuration. The validation will run enhancement on the selected resource using the current configuration, and you can view the results.
resourceProfile.propertyPool.title: Linked properties
resourceProfile.propertyPool.description: Link commonly used properties to resources matching this profile and customize their value-source priority when needed.
resourceProfile.propertyPool.empty: No linked properties yet. Choose the properties you use often.
resourceProfile.globalScopePriority.desc: Drag to adjust the display priority of property value sources. Higher priority sources will be preferred when displaying property values. This applies to all properties without a custom priority override.
resourceProfile.scopePriority.customizeT: Customize value display priority for this property, overriding the global setting
resourceProfile.page.description: Apply shared properties, display names, playback settings and metadata enhancement to matching resources.
resourceProfile.page.howItWorks: How do matching profiles work together?
resourceProfile.page.selectedHint: Configure each area independently. Other matching profiles can supply settings left unspecified here.
resourceProfile.status.inherit: Unspecified here; use another matching profile or the default behavior.
resourceProfile.status.defaultPlayer: Use another matching profile, or the system default app if none applies.
resourceProfile.empty.title: Create settings that fit your resources
resourceProfile.empty.description: For example, link director and year to movies and choose video files and players, or link authors and metadata sources to comics.
resourceProfile.tip.enhancerMerge: Metadata enhancement combines different enhancers from matching profiles. For the same enhancer, the highest-priority full configuration applies. Saving a profile does not run enhancement.
resourceProfile.tip.scope: Matching resources can use these settings. Without filters, this profile applies to all resources.
resourceProfile.tip.playback: First identify playable files within resources, then choose the apps that open them.
resourceProfile.tip.enhancers: Choose metadata sources and map their results to resource properties. Run enhancement from resources or workflows after saving.

resourceProfile.scopePriority.orderHint: Earlier sources take priority. If a source has no value, the next one is used. Drag or use the arrows to reorder.
resourceProfile.globalScopePriority.scop: This applies to all properties that use global priority, beyond the current profile. Existing resource or profile overrides remain unchanged. Changes take effect after saving.

resourceProfile.players.description: Choose the applications that open playable files and the file types each application handles.
resourceProfile.players.deviceHint: The playback device must be able to access the application and file paths. Configuring the server does not automatically launch a player on the browser's device.
resourceProfile.players.selectionOrder: Match extensions in list order, then use a player without extension restrictions, then the system default app.
resourceProfile.players.emptyTitle: No players specified for this profile
resourceProfile.players.emptyDescription: Other matching profiles can provide player settings; otherwise the system default app is used.
resourceProfile.players.pathHint: Select an application file or an existing shortcut.

resourceProfile.players.extensionsHint: Separate extensions with spaces or new lines. Leave empty to handle files without an extension-specific player.
resourceProfile.players.previewHint: Choose a file to preview and copy the launch command. This does not run the player.
resourceProfile.players.completeBeforeSa: Select an application file for each entry or remove incomplete entries before saving.
resourceProfile.players.copyFailed: Could not copy. Select and copy the command manually.
resourceProfile.playable.description: Identify playable files in local resources: match extensions first, then optionally filter file names.
resourceProfile.playable.presetsHint: Add common extensions without replacing existing entries or adding duplicates.
resourceProfile.playable.extensionsHint: Separate extensions with spaces or new lines. Matching is case-insensitive and requires at least one extension.
resourceProfile.playable.patternHint: Use a .NET regular expression to narrow files that match the extensions. It matches the file name only, ignoring case.
resourceProfile.playable.patternNeedsExt: Add an extension first. A file name pattern cannot identify playable files on its own.
resourceProfile.playable.emptyDescriptio: This profile does not define playable files yet. Saving an empty configuration removes this setting, so other matching profiles may still apply.
resourceProfile.nameEditor.description: Combine property placeholders and fixed text to name resources. Search and insert properties below, or edit the template directly.
resourceProfile.nameEditor.emptyFallback: Leave empty to use a name template from another matching profile, or the default name if none applies.
resourceProfile.nameEditor.previewHint: Colors distinguish properties, wrappers and unknown property names. This preview does not substitute actual resource values.
resourceProfile.nameEditor.unknownProper: {{count}} property name(s) are unrecognized. Check the names or insert properties below.

resourceProfile.basic.description: Give this resource profile a recognizable name and set its application priority.
resourceProfile.basic.priorityHint: Higher numbers take priority. Each setting uses the highest-priority applicable value from matching profiles.
resourceProfile.basic.newScopeHint: A new profile matches all resources by default. After creating it, the scope editor opens so you can choose which resources it should match.

resourceProfile.preview.title: Match preview
resourceProfile.preview.description: This only previews resources matching the current criteria; it does not modify them. Name, property, playback and other settings each follow the priority of matching profiles.
